clue.text: Bill a cleric? Exactly right

parts.note: AC is short for account, and a bill is an account owed
a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man called Bill is a churchman, and is told that is exactly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precise and free of error is correct in every detail.

clue.text: It is the current fashion to tear round avoiding extremes

parts.note: the mode is whatever style is in vogue now

indicators.note: turned round, the letters of tear are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that ripping things around is the latest trend, set against a call for restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges TEAR into RATE, which follows MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate position keeps to the middle ground, shunning anything excessive.

clue.text: See codes i.e. explained

indicators.note: when something is explained it is laid out afresh, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling the reader to look at a list of codes, with the abbreviation spelled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explained' rearranges the letters of CODES and IE. 'See' looks like an instruction to look; it is a noun, a bishop's district.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the territory under that bishop's charge, a church district.

clue.text: Left without officer at bazaar worn out

indicators.note: without means the word Left loses some of its letters here

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a military officer
a fete is an outdoor fundraising sale or fair

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned at a charity sale without a senior officer ends up exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes L and T from LEFT, leaving EF.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and drained of vigour, spent.

clue.text: Girl at home in new role

indicators.note: in places the home word inside the rearranged letters
a new version of the word role has its letters shuffled

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A woman relaxing in the house while taking on a fresh part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into ELOR, and 'in' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is a female first name, as in Austen's Elinor Dashwood.

clue.text: Station collapses in Africa

definitions.note: the definition places the answer, a landmark on the Zambezi

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
falls means tumbles down, as a building collapses

explanation.surface: News that a railway station has fallen down somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: VICTORIA is a big London rail terminus; the whole name is the great waterfall between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterfall on the Zambezi is one of the best-known natural sights of the continent.

clue.text: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking

definitions.text: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking

parts.words: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking
parts.note: a performer who throws the voice so the words seem to come from a dummy across the stage

explanation.surface: A description of someone who sounds aloof and evasive in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a performer makes speech appear to come from somewhere other than their own mouth.

clue.text: Roused by a bee perhaps

parts.note: the idiom for being spurred into activity, read literally as being jolted by an insect's sting

explanation.surface: Someone jolted awake by an insect buzzing nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means provoked into sudden activity, and literally a bee's sting would do that.

clue.text: At home certain to take cover

parts.note: being in means being at home
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone staying indoors, confident it is the safest way to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a policy is to arrange protection against loss.

clue.text: Neat gash has no dirt in it

definitions.text: gash has no dirt in it
definitions.meaning: a wound that is free of grime is literally an unsoiled incision

explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and wholesome in look; read literally, an incision without contamination.

clue.text: Port or whisky

definitions.meaning: One of the old Cinque Ports on the Sussex coast
whisky distilled from a cereal grain

explanation.definitionFit: A small English harbour town, and a North American spirit made from grain.

clue.text: Equip lady with a fleet of ships

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Arming a woman and giving her a navy to command.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large naval force, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Directing the course of the cheapest accommodation

definitions.meaning: guiding a vessel or vehicle along its route
the lowest-priced passenger quarters on an old ship

explanation.definitionFit: Both the act of steering and the bottom class of passage on a liner.

clue.text: Being a bit tetchy-and the rest

indicators.note: a bit of the word tetchy is taken, letters lifted from inside it

explanation.surface: Being slightly irritable, and so on and so forth.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation of et cetera stands for further things of the same kind.

clue.text: Found in or under a railway carriage

definitions.text: Found in or under a railway carriage

parts.words: Found in or under a railway carriage
parts.note: a berth car with beds travels on the line, and the wooden beams supporting the rails lie beneath the train

explanation.surface: A lost-property note about something discovered aboard or beneath a train.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an overnight train car with beds and the timber tie that holds the track.

clue.text: Its contents will be very much alike

definitions.text: Its contents will be very much alike

parts.words: Its contents will be very much alike
parts.note: from the saying about two peas looking identical, this is the casing they grow in

explanation.surface: A remark that whatever is inside some container is uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas from one seed case are proverbially identical.

clue.text: Disturbance in court

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An uproar breaking out during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance' signals an anagram of IN COURT and also defines the answer, an uproar such as one that might break out in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy row or commotion.

clue.text: In fun be a tennis player not having suffered defeat

indicators.note: In tells the solver the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a game of tennis who has never lost a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A team or player with no losses has never been beaten.

clue.text: Cross right over a few lines

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: a verse is a short run of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Instructions to strike through a short passage of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a place is to travel across it.

clue.text: Detains eccentric as an alternative

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, so these letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Locking up an oddball rather than someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute.

clue.text: Cavalry division form working party with Ronald

parts.note: a squad is a small group assigned to a task
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A man called Ronald joins up to create a work gang.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army a squadron is a unit of cavalry or armoured troops.

clue.text: Crafty paintings almost complete

parts.note: art covers paintings and similar works

indicators.note: almost means the synonym stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: full means complete, filled up

explanation.surface: A set of pictures is nearly finished, done with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final L of FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful and crafty both describe cunning, skilful deceit.

clue.text: Nothing more than an American farm hut

indicators.note: more than means the zero comes in addition, tacked onto the end

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm in the US
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dismissive description of a Western farmstead as no better than a shack.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish America a rancho is a rough hut or shelter for herders.

clue.text: Bachelor of Law goes to an ecclesiastical establishment to become pale

parts.note: BL is the degree abbreviation for Bachelor of Law
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A law graduate goes into a church and turns white with fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch is to lose colour, as a face drains with shock.

clue.text: Girl is confident without right

indicators.note: without means the word for confident is left lacking a letter

parts.note: to be sure is to be confident

explanation.surface: A woman sure of herself despite being in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a female first name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Clearly seen to be separate

explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and easy to make out, and also individual or apart from the rest.

clue.text: A meal I cooked for a girl

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed and prepared afresh

explanation.surface: Someone describing a dinner they prepared for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a female first name.

clue.text: Made to learn the hard way presumably

definitions.text: Made to learn the hard way presumably

parts.words: Made to learn the hard way presumably
parts.note: the idiom for being punished into understanding, read literally as having been given schooling

explanation.surface: Someone forced to acquire wisdom through painful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means punished so that a mistake is not repeated, and literally means instructed in class.
